review_candidates.title: Global Mobility and Benefits Specialist
review_candidates.description: Just imagine your future with us… At Aurecon we see the future through a very different lens. Do you? Innovation, eminence and digital are at the heart of everything we do. Are you excited about the future? Are you driven by the opportunity to work on some of the most challenging and complex projects around the world and to learn from the best? We are. Diversity is at the core of everything we do. We work together to create a culture based on respect, trust and inclusiveness. Our differences are what fuel our creativity. What will you do? The Global Mobility & Benefits Specialist supports the delivery of Global Mobility and Benefits services across Australia, New Zealand and Asia. The role combines end-to-end mobility case management with operational benefits administration, helping provide a consistent employee experience, accurate people data and timely service delivery. As a Global Mobility & Benefits Specialist, the role independently manages defined cases and activities within established policies and processes, applies sound judgement, coordinates internal and external stakeholders, identifies service improvements and escalates exceptions or complex matters to the advisor or team leader. Here are the key things you will do to ‘bring ideas to life’: Global Mobility Manage assigned mobility cases from initiation to completion, acting as the key operational contact for employees, candidates and relevant stakeholders. Provide first-line guidance on Global Mobility frameworks, policies and processes, escalating policy exceptions and complex matters appropriately. Prepare mobility cost estimates and package information, coordinate required approvals, and monitor actual costs against estimates. Coordinate immigration, relocation and taxation services through external providers, monitoring service delivery and resolving operational issues. Coordinate mobility documentation, employment inputs, start dates and employee-change notifications with relevant internal teams. Maintain accurate case records, approvals and supporting documentation, and manage relevant mobility mailbox activity. Validate mobility vendor invoices and support visa, work-right and related compliance activities. Benefits Administration Support the administration of local and regional employee benefits programs and platforms across Australia, New Zealand and Asia. Respond to employee and stakeholder benefits queries, providing operational guidance and escalating complex or policy-related matters as required. Maintain accurate and current benefits data in Workday and other approved systems. Coordinate with regional People teams and external providers in administering health insurance and other local benefit arrangements. Prepare benefits usage reports and operational insights, identifying trends, data issues and opportunities for improvement. Maintain benefits information and collateral, including intranet and vendor content. Support benefits surveys, recognition-program administration, approved benefits initiatives and employee communications. Shared Responsibilities Build effective relationships with employees, leaders, People teams, Payroll, Talent Acquisition, Technology teams and external providers. Maintain confidentiality, data accuracy and appropriate information handling across all activities. Identify practical improvements to processes, documentation, reporting and technology. Work flexibly across Mobility and Benefits priorities to support service delivery and business continuity. Undertake other duties and responsibilities as reasonably assigned to support evolving business requirements. What can you bring to the team? Skills Firstly, strong sense of responsibility, flexibility, and adaptability to varying request. Demonstrate excellent time management and organisational skills. And as part of a new team, you will have the opportunity to shape this role and have input into how we evolve it over time to WOW our employees and make an even bigger impact on the world. You will also need the following: Minimum three (3) years of relevant HR, Global Mobility, Remuneration, Benefits, or shared-services experience preferred. Demonstrated understanding of global mobility practices, including immigration, relocation, tax coordination and employee case management. Knowledge of benefits administration, or demonstrated ability to build capability in this area. Experience working across multiple countries, ideally including Australia, New Zealand or Asia. Tertiary qualification in Human Resources, Business or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience. Competence in Microsoft Office applications; Workday experience is preferred. Experience in a global or matrixed shared-services environment is desirable. Our Aurecon Attributes describe the types of people we bring together for clients. We don’t expect you to have all eight of the attributes, but one that is unique to you. Finally, we value that each of our team members brings something different to Aurecon. We look for people who have had a broad range of experiences throughout their career and can demonstrate how they have worked as part of a team to bring ideas to life. Does that sound like you? About Us We’ve re-imagined engineering. Aurecon is an engineering and infrastructure advisory company, but not as you know it! For a start, our clients’ ideas drive what we do. Drawing on our deep pool of expertise, we co-create innovative solutions with our clients to some of the world’s most complex challenges. And through a range of unique creative processes and skills, we work to re-imagine, shape and design a better future. We listen deeply and intently, which helps us see opportunities, possibilities and potential that others can’t. Think engineering. Think again. Want to know more? You can learn more about what it’s like to work at Aurecon by visiting the careers section of our website. If you are intrigued or excited by what you have read, then we want to hear from you. Apply now!

review_candidates.description: Background JOB DESCRIPTION UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. Summary Of Country Profile The armed conflict in Sudan, now in its fourth year, has resulted in the world’s largest humanitarian crisis, with an estimated 33.7 million people in need of humanitarian assistance, and more than 8.6 million internally displaced across all 18 states, amid acute food insecurity, near-collapse of basic services and repeated attacks on civilians, particularly in Darfur and Kordofan. Women and girls bear a disproportionate burden and impact of the conflict. Sexual violence has been used systematically as a weapon of war, and the number of women and girls needing gender-based violence (GBV) services has quadrupled since the conflict began. Women-led organizations (WLOs) are at the forefront of the humanitarian response and local peacebuilding, often reaching communities that others actors cannot access. In 2025, 85 WLOs surveyed by UN Women reported supporting more than 17.5 million people, underscoring their critical role in delivering assistance, strengthening community resilience and advancing locally led peacebuilding. Yet, despite their contribution, WLOs continue to face significant funding and capacity constraints, with limited access to humanitarian financing and continued exclusion from formal peace processes. Against this backdrop, aligned to the UN Women Strategic Plan, relevant regional and country planning frameworks, and the Sudan UN Interim Cooperation Framework, the UN Women Sudan Country Office implements programmes across the country. Guided by the UN Women Sudan Strategic Note 2026–2028, the country office prioritizes women’s leadership and meaningful participation in peace processes and mediation; gender in humanitarian action (GiHA) and coordination; prevention of and response to GBV and conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV); women’s economic empowerment and resilient livelihoods for displaced and host-community women; and strengthening and resourcing women led organizations, including through the Women, Peace and Humanitarian Fund (WPHF).UN Women Sudan plays a strategic role in advancing the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agenda, strengthening gender-responsive humanitarian action, and ensuring that women's leadership, priorities and rights are integrated into peacebuilding, recovery and development processes. The Country Office works through national institutions, women-led organizations, civil society networks and UN system coordination mechanisms to strengthen local leadership, accountability and sustainable results in an exceptionally complex operating environment. Under the overall supervision of UN Women Regional Director for East and Southern Africa, the Country Representative is responsible for providing strategic direction to advancing gender equality and women's empowerment across the humanitarian-development-peace nexus in Sudan. The Country Representative positions UN Women strategically within the UNCT, HCT and broader international engagement on Sudan, while strengthening partnerships with national and local actors, regional institutions and international partners. As a UNCT member, the Country Representative has mutual accountability with the Resident Coordinator for periodically reporting on contributions to, and support for the implementation of the United Nations Interim Cooperation Framework (UNICF), including substantive contribution to the Sudan Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) and the UNCT-SWAP Gender Equality Scorecard, among other planning and gender accountability frameworks. The Country Representative is responsible for leading and managing the Sudan Country Office (CO) portfolio and for translating the UN Women's Strategic Plan (SP) into humanitarian, peacebuilding and development initiatives and results by developing, implementing and managing programmes and projects under the Sudan CO; and developing effective partnerships with Government counterparts, UN system agencies and organizations, civil society and women led organizations, and with bilateral and non-traditional donors in order to promote inter-agency partnerships, support for UN reform, and mobilization of visibility and resources to advance gender equality and women's empowerment. Key Functions And Accountabilities Manage the strategic country programme planning and development: Develop and implement the strategic direction of UN Women in Sudan, adapting it to the evolving conflict, humanitarian and political context; Lead the design, planning and development of the Country Strategic Note in close consultation and collaboration with the government, civil society, donors, UN system partners and the Regional Director, Resident/Humanitarian Coordinator in the country and other national development stakeholders and partners, taking into account national priorities, and the Country Analysis and UNICF, the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan, and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), among others. Provide substantive advice to the UN Women Executive Director, Regional Director and Senior Management on the country strategy, direction, planning and implementation of programmes and projects in the country; Manage and ensure high quality, results and rights-based programming for the CO; Lead the monitoring and reporting of the results under the Country Office Strategic Note; Define and assert accountability for UN Women’s results and its ability to operate as a nimble, innovative and enterprising thought leader, programme and business partner capable of taking and managing risks; Ensure strategic integration of humanitarian, development, peacebuilding and recovery programming, applying the humanitarian-development-peace nexus and promoting coherent, conflict-sensitive and gender-responsive interventions; Ensure that the Country Office's programme portfolio is evidence-based, results-oriented, responsive to changing needs and supported by robust monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning mechanisms; Provide strategic oversight of programme performance, expenditure, delivery and achievement of results, ensuring timely corrective action where implementation, financial or operational challenges arise. Lead Enterprise Risk Management and Organizational Resilience: Establish and maintain the CO's risk management framework in alignment with UN Women's Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) policy and institutional risk appetite; Lead regular risk assessments covering programmatic, operational, financial, reputational, fraud, safeguarding, and security risks; ensure risks are identified, assessed, monitored and mitigated; Chair or designate the Country Office Risk Focal Point; ensure risk register is regularly updated and escalated to Regional Office as appropriate; Integrate risk considerations into strategic planning, programme design, partner due diligence, and resource allocation decisions; Ensure implementation of internal control frameworks and compliance with UN Women's policies on fraud prevention, anti-corruption, and protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA); Oversee business continuity planning and organizational resilience measures to ensure programme continuity during crises or disruptions Monitor external risk factors (political, economic, social, environmental) that may impact programme delivery and organizational operations; develop mitigation strategies; Ensure adequate risk transfer mechanisms (insurance, contractual protections) are in place for major programmes and partnerships; Promote an organizational culture of transparency, accountability, ethical conduct and proactive risk management. Manage the Sudan Country Office; Lead the office in the delivery of operational goals; annual work plan and budget; and oversee the implementation, providing direction, guidance and technical support; Review and manage high-risk transactions, partnerships, and programmatic decisions; Oversee and approve programme work plans and monitor the overall progress and compliance of the CO; Manage the preparation of UN Women mandated country reports; Manage audit review processes including timely response to audit reports; oversee implementation of audit recommendations and corrective action plans; ensure systematic tracking and closure of audit findings; proactively address recurring or systemic control weaknesses; Provide managerial direction, guidance and leadership. Ensure effective workforce planning and timely recruitment; manage the performance of personnel under their supervision; provide ongoing performance and career development feedback, timely completion of performance assessments and coaching; Ensure that personnel are familiar with and follow UN Women’s regulations and rules, policies and procedures in the Policy, Procedures and Guidance Framework (PPG); Ensure personnel are aware in particular or of UN Women’s standards of conduct including but not limited to policies and procedures on preventing, reporting and addressing misconduct, Fraud and Corruption, Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) Harassment, Sexual Harassment, Discrimination and abuse of authority, Protection from retaliation, and ensure mechanisms are in place to support personnel in this regard; Promote teamwork to ensure harmonization, linkages, collaboration and synergy; Ensure a respectful, inclusive safe and healthy work environment for personnel; Ensure effective financial stewardship of the Country Office portfolio, including budget management, expenditure monitoring, delivery performance, financial forecasting and appropriate resource allocation in line with institutional policies and donor agreements; Ensure effective oversight of procurement, human resources, finance, administration, ICT and other operational functions, maintaining appropriate segregation of duties and internal control mechanisms; Promote a culture of accountability for results, performance, compliance and responsible management of organizational resources; Provide strategic leadership in workforce planning, organizational restructuring, talent management and succession planning, ensuring that the Country Office has the appropriate skills, competencies and staffing arrangements to deliver its mandate in a complex and evolving operating environment; Promote teamwork to ensure harmonization, linkages, collaboration and synergy; Ensure a respectful, inclusive safe and healthy work environment for personnel. Provide support to the Resident Coordinator/ Humanitarian Coordinator and serve as a member of UN Country Team/ UN Humanitarian Country Team Serve as member of the UN Country Team (UNCT) under the strategic guidance and coordination of the UN Resident Coordinator (RC)/Humanitarian Coordinator (HC), collaborate on and lead as needed, UNCT programming and advocacy to ensure gender equality and women’s empowerment issues are fully integrated into UN programming processes, including the Country Analysis (CA) and United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) planning, budgeting, resource mobilization, implementation, monitoring and evaluation through UN results groups and respective joint workplans, and in an enhanced response to national partners; Partner with RC and UN system partners to strengthen UN system interagency coherence, collaboration, planning, cooperation, and harmonization of programming, advocacy, common services, and operations; Facilitate joint programming and promote UN competencies to advance gender equality and women’s human rights; report to the UN RC on these issues as required; Actively engage in regular UNCT consultations and decision-making processes; Actively engage in and contribute to UNCT strategic communications that advance UN system efforts and collective results to promote Agenda 2030, including for national goals and priorities for sustainable development to generate positive public support and ownership; Ensure UN Women’s active participation in UN system thematic and other working groups to establish effective networks and keep abreast of ongoing debates and thinking on development; Ensure organizational position, interests and priorities are fully considered and integrated in the UNSDCF development planning and agenda/priority setting for the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals; Ensure enhanced accountability of the UNCT on gender mainstreaming and work with the RC on the implementation of the UNCT SWAP Gender Equality Scorecard; Participate in RC and UNCT members’ performance appraisal, as requested; Provide strategic leadership and technical guidance to strengthen UN system accountability for gender equality and women's empowerment, including through the UNCT-SWAP Gender Equality Scorecard, Gender Theme Group and other inter-agency coordination mechanisms;
